entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14191"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 16</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Mark.16.1-Mark.16.20">Mr 16:1-20</reference>. Angelic Announcement to the Women on the First Day of the Week, that Christ Is Risen--His Appearances after His Resurrection--His Ascension--Triumphant Proclamation of His Gospel. ( = <reference osisRef="Matt.28.1-Matt.10.16">Mt 28:1-10, 16</reference>-20; <reference osisRef="Luke.24.1-Luke.24.51">Lu 24:1-51</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.20.1">Joh 20:1</reference>, 2, 11-29).</title> <div sID="gen27486" type="x-p"/> The Resurrection Announced to the Women (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.1-Mark.16.8">Mr 16:1-8</reference>).<div eID="gen27486" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27487" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14191"/><hi type="bold">1. And when the sabbath was past--</hi>that is, at sunset of our Saturday.<div eID="gen27487" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27488" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Mary Magdalene--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Luke.8.2">Lu 8:2</reference>).<div eID="gen27488" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27489" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and Mary the mother of James--</hi>James the Less (see <reference osisRef="Mark.15.40">Mr 15:40</reference>).<div eID="gen27489" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27490" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">and Salome--</hi>the mother of Zebedee's sons (compare <reference osisRef="Mark.15.40">Mr 15:40</reference> with <reference osisRef="Matt.27.56">Mt 27:56</reference>).<div eID="gen27490" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27491" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him--</hi>The word is simply "bought." But our translators are perhaps right in rendering it here "had bought," since it would appear, from <reference osisRef="Luke.23.56">Lu 23:56</reference>, that they had purchased them immediately after the Crucifixion, on the Friday evening, during the short interval that remained to them before sunset, when the sabbath rest began; and that they had only deferred using them to anoint the body till the sabbath rest should be over. On this "anointing," see on <reference osisRef="John.19.40">Joh 19:40</reference>. <div eID="gen27491" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 16 Mr 16:1-20 . Angelic Announcement to the Women on the First Day of the Week, that Christ Is Risen--His Appearances after His Resurrection--His Ascension--Triumphant Proclamation of His Gospel. ( = Mt 28:1-10, 16 -20; Lu 24:1-51 ; Joh 20:1 , 2, 11-29). The Resurrection Announced to the Women ( Mr 16:1-8 ). 1. And when the sabbath was past-- that is, at sunset of our Saturday. Mary Magdalene-- (See on Lu 8:2 ). and Mary the mother of James-- James the Less (see Mr 15:40 ). and Salome-- the mother of Zebedee's sons (compare Mr 15:40 with Mt 27:56 ). had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him-- The word is simply "bought." But our translators are perhaps right in rendering it here "had bought," since it would appear, from Lu 23:56 , that they had purchased them immediately after the Crucifixion, on the Friday evening, during the short interval that remained to them before sunset, when the sabbath rest began; and that they had only deferred using them to anoint the body till the sabbath rest should be over. On this "anointing," see on Joh 19:40 .

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14194"/><div sID="gen27496" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14194"/><hi type="bold">5. And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man--</hi>In <reference osisRef="Matt.28.2">Mt 28:2</reference> he is called "the angel of the Lord"; but here he is described as he appeared to the eye, in the bloom of a life that knows no decay. In Matthew he is represented as sitting on the stone outside the sepulchre; but since even there he says, "Come, see the place where the Lord lay" (<reference osisRef="Matt.28.6">Mt 28:6</reference>), he seems, as Alford says, to have gone in with them from without; only awaiting their arrival to accompany them into the hallowed spot, and instruct them about it.<div eID="gen27496" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen27497" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sitting on the right side--</hi>having respect to the position in which His Lord had lain there. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14198"/><div sID="gen27509" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14198"/><hi type="bold">9. Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils--</hi>There is some difficulty here, and different ways of removing it have been adopted. She had gone with the other women to the sepulchre (<reference osisRef="Mark.16.1">Mr 16:1</reference>), parting from them, perhaps, before their interview with the angel, and on finding Peter and John she had come with them back to the spot; and it was at this second visit, it would seem, that Jesus appeared to this Mary, as detailed in <reference osisRef="John.20.11-John.20.18">Joh 20:11-18</reference>. To a woman was this honor given to be the first that saw the risen Redeemer, and that woman was NOT his virgin-mother. <div eID="gen27509" type="x-p"/>
